metadata.title: Bitcoin's November rout echoes past crypto downturns

content.text:
Crypto stocks fell early Monday, with bitcoin's November sell-off shaping up to become one of its worst on record.
Bitcoin fell as low as $64,000, a 2% drop in the last 24 hours before paring losses. The world's largest cryptocurrency is down nearly 16% so far for November, marking the world's largest cryptocurrency's second-worst start to the month since 2016, according to Yahoo Finance data.
Only in November 2022, when the collapse of crypto exchange FTX sent shockwaves through the crypto world, was the rout through the first half of the month worse.
Shares of Robinhood (HOOD) declined 3% in Monday morning trading, while those for stablecoin issuer Circle (CRCL) fell 4%. Coinbase Global (COIN) and bitcoin buyer Strategy (MSTR) each fell 5%.
Read more: Is bitcoin's price volatility an investing opportunity?
The headwinds for the crypto world keep coming. Expectations for a tighter monetary policy by the Federal Reserve have weighed on investor appetite for riskier assets.
A number of publicly traded bitcoin miners have also accelerated their bitcoin sales during the first half of the year, according to Needham & Co.
Meanwhile, the industry faces a less-friendly Democratic majority in Washington following the midterm elections, after lawmakers failed earlier this year to advance legislation that would have cemented favorable regulatory protections. Last month, crypto exchange Binance was also hit by the industry's biggest hack on record.
Bitcoin's November decline has left it down 25% year to date, its third-worst performance through mid-November in the past decade, behind only the brutal crypto bear markets of 2018 and 2022.
The sell-off is also rekindling memories of the industry's bleakest periods.
"Crypto is giving mid-2018 vibes, when the space was exhausted, and a lot of people gave up," said Matt Hougan, chief investment officer at Bitwise Asset Management.
Hougan warned that the industry could "wander through the wilderness for a while" as investors digest the longer-term effects of the elections, the Binance hack, and tighter monetary policy.
But bitcoin's historical trading patterns suggest its latest downturn could be approaching a turning point. The cryptocurrency's last three bear markets bottomed roughly 12 to 13 months after their preceding peaks, according to a Yahoo Finance analysis by Jared Blikre.
Bitcoin is now just over 13 months removed from its October 2025 record, though past cycles offer no guarantee of another rebound.
